eyebrow: Enterprise Cloud Architecture & Advanced Capstone · Chapter 3
subtitle: Lesson 9 · Network Architecture at Enterprise Scale

steps.label: Full mesh: every network peers with every other
steps.sub: connection count grows roughly as N² — unmanageable past a handful of teams

steps.label: Hub-and-spoke: spokes only connect to the hub
steps.sub: connection count drops to roughly N, with one policy enforcement point

steps.label: VNet/VPC peering is non-transitive on both clouds
steps.sub: a spoke peered to the hub cannot auto-reach another spoke through it

eyebrow: Azure: UDRs force traffic through the hub
code:
az network route-table create \
  --resource-group hub-rg \
  --name spoke-to-hub-routes

az network route-table route create \
  --resource-group hub-rg \
  --route-table-name spoke-to-hub-routes \
  --name default-to-firewall \
  --address-prefix 0.0.0.0/0 \
  --next-hop-type VirtualAppliance \
  --next-hop-ip-address 10.0.0.4
caption: A UDR overriding 0.0.0.0/0 is what turns non-transitive peering into centralized egress.

eyebrow: AWS: Transit Gateway as a managed router
code:
aws ec2 create-transit-gateway \
  --description "enterprise-hub-tgw"

aws ec2 create-transit-gateway-vpc-attachment \
  --transit-gateway-id tgw-0123456789abcdef0 \
  --vpc-id vpc-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 \
  --subnet-ids subnet-0f1e2d3c4b5a69870
caption: Transit Gateway handles transitive routing natively through route table associations on each attachment.

steps.label: Azure: architect enforces it with UDRs on every spoke
steps.sub: scales to Virtual WAN once hand-wiring UDRs gets unwieldy

steps.label: AWS: TGW route table associations enforce it natively
steps.sub: an inspection VPC attachment can see every other attachment's traffic

steps.label: Both: one connection point, one policy, linear not quadratic
steps.sub: the architectural intent is identical even though the mechanics differ
